app.name: versorium
app.quitUnsaved: Versorium did not quit: the chapter could not be saved. {reason}

empty.title: A quiet desk, a sharp needle.
empty.body: Create a project to start writing. Everything stays on this machine.

rename.label: Title
rename.projectHint: Only the title changes. The folder keeps its name, so your backups and any GitHub remote still point at it.
rename.chapterHint: Only the title changes. The file keeps its name, which is what holds the chapter's position and its writing history.

confirm.projectBody: The whole folder goes to your system Trash, including its history. You can put it back from there until you empty it.
confirm.chapterBody: Versorium saves a snapshot first, so this chapter stays in the novel's history and can be brought back.

editor.focusHint: Clear the page of the bars ticked in Focus options. Esc brings them back. ({keys})
editor.focusNeedsChapter: Open a chapter to use Focus.
editor.focusOffNote: Takes effect when Focus is on.
editor.focusNothingNote: Nothing is ticked, so Focus only quiets the status bar.
editor.focusOn: Focus on. Press Escape to leave.
editor.typewriterHint: Keep the line you are writing at the lower third.

chrome.lipHint: Show top bar ({keys}). Rewrite works without it: {rewriteKeys}.

settings.title: Settings
settings.themeHint: Folio is warm paper, Quarry a quieter warm grey, Needle cool with a teal cast. Each one has a light and a dark version; the mode below decides which you see.
settings.languageHint: Changes the interface only. It never touches the language your novel is written in.

purpose.editor: How the page looks and behaves while you write: typeface, spelling, the size and spacing of the text, line numbers, the current-paragraph highlight, and what the Tab key does.
purpose.author: Who the manuscript is by, as the exported file will say it.
purpose.appearance: How Versorium looks, and what language its own buttons speak.
purpose.localAi: Which model does each job, and where those models come from. Nothing here sends your prose anywhere.
purpose.backup: Your novel's history on this disk, and an optional private copy on GitHub. Versorium never mixes it with its own repository.
purpose.assistants: Assistants that reach into your novel from outside, and exactly how much each one is allowed to do.
purpose.app: Versorium itself: the version you are running, how it updates, and what it records when it crashes.

git.title: History
git.dirty: There are changes not in a snapshot yet
git.commitHint: Save a snapshot of this chapter and the project. You can come back to it.
git.updatesSlotHint: Only needed while maecly/versorium-app is private, or to lift GitHub's hourly limit on checks without a token.
git.novelSlotHint: Used only for your novel's own private backup. Never for updates.
git.noToken: Paste a GitHub personal access token to set up the backup.
git.advancedNote: Versorium keeps your novel's history in Git. These are Git's own controls — you never need them to write.
git.restoreHint: Put the selection back as it was, or the word under the cursor when nothing is selected.
git.storedWhere: Stored in your system's credential store, never in a file.

errors.projectExists: A project with that name already exists.
errors.project_exists: A project with that name already exists.
errors.no_repo: This folder is not keeping history yet.
errors.nothing_to_commit: Nothing has changed since the last snapshot.
errors.network: Network error while talking to GitHub.
errors.repo_failed: GitHub could not create the repository.
errors.branch_exists: A branch with that name already exists.
errors.bad_range: That passage is outside the chapter.
errors.stale_selection: The passage changed since you selected it. Select it again.
errors.mcp_config_failed: Versorium could not write that client's config file.
errors.no_home: Could not locate your home folder.
errors.download_busy: Another model is already downloading. Wait for it to finish.
errors.sha_mismatch: The download did not match its checksum, so it was deleted. Try again.
errors.not_ready: Download that model before selecting it.
errors.bad_catalog: The model catalog could not be read.
errors.bad_args: That value is not one Versorium accepts.
errors.bad_format: Versorium does not know that format.
errors.unsupported_source: Versorium cannot read that kind of file.
errors.empty_manuscript: There is nothing to export yet.
errors.no_author: This format needs an author for its running heads.
errors.import_prose_before_first_chapter: Text before the first chapter heading was kept as an opening chapter.
errors.import_no_chapter_headings: No chapter headings were found, so the whole document became one chapter.
errors.import_title_guessed: The title was taken from the first heading.
errors.import_not_utf8: Some characters could not be decoded and were replaced.
errors.import_scrivener_labels_dropped: Scrivener labels and status flags were not carried across.
errors.import_scrivener_notes_dropped: Scrivener document notes were not carried across.
errors.import_docx_formatting_dropped: Bold, italics and other formatting were not carried across.
errors.import_docx_no_headings: No Heading 1 was found, so the whole document became one chapter.
errors.empty_document: That file has no text to import.
errors.export_pdf_characters_replaced: Some characters cannot be printed in a PDF and were replaced.
errors.export_docx_scene_titles_dropped: Scene titles are not part of manuscript format; the scene breaks remain.
errors.no_manifest: That release has no update manifest attached.
errors.update_none_visible: No published version is visible yet: either nothing has been released, or the repository is still private and no token that can read it is saved.
errors.update_rate_limited: GitHub's limit on update checks without a token has been reached. An updates token, saved in Settings → Application, lifts it.
errors.update_rate_limited_token: GitHub's rate limit for this updates token has been reached.
errors.update_token_rejected: GitHub refused the updates token: it is wrong or has been revoked. Replace it or forget it in Settings → Application.
errors.bad_signature: The update's signature did not verify, so nothing was installed.
errors.no_checksums: The release has no checksum for this download, so nothing was installed.
errors.unsupported_platform: Versorium cannot update itself on this operating system or processor.
errors.bad_update_host: The update pointed somewhere unexpected and was refused.
errors.continuity_no_model: No model is selected for Continuity. Pick one under Local AI.
errors.continuity_daemon_offline: The Ollama daemon is not running, so the check could not start.
errors.continuity_failed: The continuity check could not finish.
errors.no_runtime: Versorium has no engine for that task yet. Dictation needs a speech model, which llama.cpp cannot run.
errors.ollama_offline: Ollama is not answering. Start it and try again.
errors.llama_busy: Versorium is already running one model. Wait for it to finish.
errors.llama_load_failed: That model file could not be loaded. It may be for a different purpose than writing.
errors.llama_failed: The local model could not finish that.
errors.model_too_large: That model needs more memory than this machine has. Pick a smaller one.
errors.continuity_busy: A rewrite is running. The continuity check waits rather than competing for the model.
errors.continuity_model_too_large: The model chosen for Continuity needs more memory than this machine has.
errors.git_auth_failed: GitHub refused that token. Check it under Settings → History & backup.
errors.git_behind_remote: The copy on GitHub has changes this one does not. Pull first.
errors.git_diverged: Both copies changed separately. Versorium cannot merge that yet — open the folder in a git tool.
errors.no_remote: This novel has no GitHub backup set up yet.
errors.export_scrivener_scenes_flattened: Scene breaks become a separator: Scrivener has no scene inside a document.
errors.import_epub_styles_dropped: The book's styling is not kept: a Versorium chapter is Markdown.
errors.mcp_http_bind_failed: Versorium could not open a local port for HTTP.
errors.mcp_http_no_entropy: Versorium could not get random bytes from the operating system, so it will not open an HTTP port with a guessable token.
errors.trash_failed: Versorium could not move that to the Trash.
errors.remote_not_github: This project's remote is not a GitHub address, so the token was not sent. Versorium only signs in to github.com over https.
errors.backup_not_configured: No backup folder has been chosen.
errors.backup_dest_missing: That folder is not there any more.
errors.backup_dest_unwritable: The folder doesn't accept new files: it is read-only, or Versorium has no permission.
errors.backup_write_failed: The archive could not be written.
errors.backup_unreadable: The archive could not be read back.
errors.backup_corrupt: The archive did not read back intact.
errors.repo_busy: A backup is reading the novel's history. Try again in a moment.

ai.noProviders: No assistant found. Install Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Ollama, then check again in Settings → Assistants.
ai.checkpointNote: Versorium snapshots Git before applying. You can roll back.
ai.creativeSoon: Creative mode is coming. It is not available yet.

agents.title: Assistants on this machine
agents.hint: Found, not configured: each one keeps its own login and Versorium never stores their keys. Versorium can hand a task to one of these when no local model is assigned to it.
agents.ollamaOffline: Binary found, daemon offline. Start Ollama to connect.
agents.none: Agent detection runs inside the desktop app.

safety.title: Safety
safety.censorshipHint: On, models marked uncensored are hidden from the list above. That is all it does today: it does not change what any assistant is asked, and nothing routes requests by it.

mcp.title: What they are allowed to do
mcp.intro: The arrow points the other way here: an assistant connects to Versorium and reads your manuscript through it. A local server on this machine — over stdio, and over HTTP only if you turn it on below — read-only until you allow writing, per client.
mcp.commandHint: Connected clients spawn this. Nothing listens on the network.
mcp.writeWarning: Write lets the AI change your manuscript. Versorium will snapshot Git first. You can roll back. The model can still delete text if you allow the edit.
mcp.logHint: Records tool names, clients and paths. Never your manuscript text.
mcp.restartHint: Restart {client} for the change to take effect.
mcp.none: The MCP server runs inside the desktop app.
mcp.httpHint: Some assistants cannot start a program and need a URL instead. Versorium listens on this machine only, on a port it picks, and a client must present a token it reads from a file only you can open.
mcp.httpOff: Off. Assistants reach Versorium by starting it, which needs no network at all.
mcp.httpFile: The URL and token are here
mcp.httpRestart: Turning this off takes effect next time Versorium starts.

localAi.title: Local AI
localAi.intro: Models that run on this machine. Nothing leaves it.
localAi.none: Local models run inside the desktop app.

wizard.title: This machine
wizard.recommended: With {ram} of memory, the {tier} pack is the largest that fits comfortably.
wizard.hint: Nothing downloads on its own. Pick a model when you want it.

card.tooBig: Larger than this machine can hold comfortably. You can still download it.
card.corrupt: The file on disk does not match its checksum. Delete it and download again.
card.empty: The catalog has no models for this tab yet.
card.ladderIntro: These all do the same work: rewriting, chat and continuity. They differ in quality, speed and memory. Pick the largest one your machine can hold.
card.uncensoredWhy: Safety filter removed, for fiction a filtered model refuses to help with.

purpose.writing: Rewrites a passage, talks about the manuscript, checks continuity.
purpose.embeddings: Does not write. Turns your chapters into vectors so search finds meaning, not just matching words.

tierNote.low: The lightest. A fast draft on a modest machine.
tierNote.mid: The sweet spot on an ordinary laptop.
tierNote.midPlus: Noticeably better prose, and it is heavy.
tierNote.high: The best here, and it asks for a lot of memory.

ollama.notInstalled: The ollama binary was not found on this machine.
ollama.installHint: Install Ollama and start it, then refresh.
ollama.offlineHint: Ollama is installed but its daemon is not answering. Start it, then refresh.

studio.intro: LM Studio or llama-server, anything speaking the OpenAI API on this machine. You can test and save the connection now; assigning it to a task is not built yet.

dictation.intro: Dictate into the open chapter with a local Whisper model.
dictation.soon: The Whisper packs arrive in a later milestone. The downloader they will use is already here.

slots.title: What each model is used for
slots.intro: Pick a model per task. A task with no model falls back to a connected agent.
slots.embeddingsHint: Indexing the manuscript so search understands meaning.

engine.title: Engine
engine.warming: starting… (compiling GPU shaders, once per machine)
engine.failed: llama.cpp could not start on this machine.
engine.noGpuBuild: · this build has no GPU backend, so speeds are CPU speeds

filter.noMatch: No model matches that. Clear the search or the filters.

tasks.title: What each task uses
tasks.intro: Five jobs, and the model each one runs on. A task with no model falls back to a connected assistant — and if there is none, it says so rather than doing nothing.

sources.title: Where models come from
sources.intro: Where a model can come from. Built-in and Ollama models can be given to the tasks above; a local server can be configured here but no task can use it yet.

export.title: Export
export.intro: Write the whole manuscript out as one file.

formats.md: The canonical format. Nothing is lost.
formats.docx: Standard manuscript format: 12pt serif, double-spaced, 1-inch margins, surname / title / page in the header.
formats.pdf: Print preview, with chapter openings and running heads.
formats.scriv: A Scrivener 3 project folder, one document per chapter.

export.author: Author
export.authorHint: DOCX and PDF print the surname in every running head, so they need it.
export.authorMissing: Add an author to export this format.
export.warningsTitle: This format could not carry everything:

import.title: Import
import.intro: Read a manuscript into a new project. Nothing is written until you confirm.
import.warningsTitle: What this import cannot carry across

updates.title: Updates
updates.intro: Versorium checks its own releases. Nothing about your manuscript is sent.
updates.offline: GitHub could not be reached, or did not answer as expected, so nothing was checked.
updates.automaticHint: Check once at launch. On by default on the stable channel.
updates.channelHint: Beta is opt-in and ships unfinished work.
updates.offlineHint: A failed check is left alone — no pop-up, no retry loop.
updates.gatekeeper: Builds are signed with minisign, but not yet notarized by Apple or Microsoft, so the first launch may warn you.
updates.none: Updates are handled by the desktop app.

dialog.title: A new version of Versorium
dialog.heading: Version {version} is ready
dialog.noNotes: This release came with no notes.
dialog.verified: Versorium checks the signature and the checksum before replacing anything. If either fails, nothing is installed.

phase.readyHint: Restart to open the new version.

onboarding.title: Welcome to Versorium
onboarding.machineSummary: {ram} of memory and {cores} cores. The {tier} pack is the largest that fits comfortably.
onboarding.machineUnknown: Versorium could not read this machine's memory. You can still pick a model later.
onboarding.machineHint: Nothing is downloaded here. Models are chosen in Settings, when you want them.
onboarding.agentsHint: Versorium uses the AI tools you already have. Each keeps its own login — no keys are stored here.
onboarding.agentsNone: No agent tools were found. Versorium works without them; you can add one later.
onboarding.projectHint: A novel is a plain folder on your disk, keeping its own history from the first save.
onboarding.projectCreated: Created. Your novel is on disk and under version control.
onboarding.templateHint: A structure only seeds chapter titles. Versorium never writes prose you did not ask for.
onboarding.firstSceneBody: That is everything. Your manuscript is Markdown on your disk, and it never leaves this machine unless you send it somewhere.
onboarding.rewriteHint: Select a passage and press Rewrite to hand it to an agent. You see the diff before anything changes.
onboarding.none: Setup runs inside the desktop app.
onboarding.replayHint: The short tour from the first run: this machine, what it found, and a novel to start from.

typography.intro: What the editor renders your prose in.
typography.sample: El invierno fue largo, y la niña esperaba junto a la ventana.
typography.downloadLater: Downloadable families arrive with the font downloader in a later release. Nothing here needs fetching.
typography.none: Typography is handled by the desktop app.

spelling.title: Spelling
spelling.label: Check spelling as you type
spelling.hint: Your system's spelling checker underlines the words it does not know. Nothing is changed for you: right-click a word to see suggestions.
spelling.hintLinux: On Linux nothing is underlined yet: Versorium does not switch the system's spelling checker on there. Your choice is kept for when it does.

guides.title: Guides
guides.lineNumbersHint: Numbers each line of the chapter as the editor shows it, blank ones included. A paragraph counts as one line, however far it wraps.
guides.activeLineHint: A faint band behind the paragraph the cursor is in.

keyboard.title: Keyboard
keyboard.tabHint: Exports ignore the indent. Indented twice, a paragraph becomes a code block in the chapter file, and its italics stop showing.

crash.title: Crash reports
crash.privacy: Crash files stay on this machine and carry no manuscript text — only the version, the platform and where the code stopped. Nothing is sent unless you press Report.
crash.none: Crash reports are handled by the desktop app.
crash.reviewHint: The issue opens prefilled. Read it before you post — you can cut anything you would rather not share.

continuity.title: Continuity check
continuity.hint: Reads the manuscript against itself for contradictions. A stub: it needs a local model selected for the Continuity task.
continuity.none: The continuity check runs inside the desktop app.

backup.title: Backup
backup.intro: Three copies of a manuscript, on two kinds of storage, one of them somewhere else. That rule is older than cloud sync and it is still the whole of it. Versorium keeps the first copy as the novel's own history, and writes dated archives — history included — into every folder you pick below.
backup.finished: The backup has finished; the list below is up to date.
backup.notSavedFirst: Not backed up: the chapter could not be saved first. {reason}
backup.restoreHint: Restoring extracts a copy beside this novel. Nothing you have now is overwritten.
backup.limit: Pick up to {n}. Past that, the slowest one decides how long every backup takes.
backup.full: Three destinations is the limit. Remove one to add another.
backup.layerHistoryHint: Every snapshot you save is kept inside the novel's folder. It survives a mistake, not a lost laptop.
backup.hasOffsite: one of them off this machine
backup.noOffsite: none of them off this machine
backup.sameDisk: {path} is on the same disk as the novel — if that disk fails, both go.
backup.resultUnavailable: {name}: not reachable right now. Press Back up now again once it is connected.
backup.resultBusy: {name}: skipped, because the novel's history was being written. Press Back up now again in a moment.
backup.verified: Read back in full and intact.
backup.verifyHint: Checking opens the archive and reads every file back. An archive that has sat on a disk for a year is the one this is for.
backup.liveRepoHint: The novel itself stays where it is. A live repository inside a synced folder gets corrupted — these services copy file by file, with no regard for the order git needs.
backup.resultUnchanged: {name}: nothing has changed since {when}. Nothing new was written; that copy was read back in full and is intact.
backup.resultCopy: {name}: nothing has changed, so this is a second copy of the same state, {size}. There will not be a third.
backup.resultRepaired: {name}: the copy that was there could not be read back in full. A new one was written, {size}. The damaged file was left where it is.
backup.alsoPruned: {n} older ones were deleted to stay within the number you keep.
backup.onlyWhenChanged: Back up now writes a new archive only when the novel has changed. It keeps two copies of each state at each destination, then tells you instead of writing — pressing it again cannot fill the folder.
backup.keepHint: Archives, not days. With two copies of each state, ten archives is at least five different states of the novel.

held.clockBehind: A backup here is dated {stamp}, later than this computer's clock, so no backups were deleted. Check the date and time on this computer and on any other that backs up here, or remove that file yourself.

author.title: Author
author.intro: What goes inside the exported file, not on the page. Readers, libraries and publishers all look here first, and a file with an empty author is one nobody can attribute.
author.none: Author details need the desktop app.

profiles.workHint: The name on a contract: legal name, publisher, the copyright line they gave you.
profiles.hobbyHint: A pen name, a pseudonym, work that is nobody's business but yours.

where.name: The byline. Written as the author into EPUB, DOCX, PDF and Markdown. A project that already has its own author keeps it.
where.sortAs: How a library shelves it — surname first. EPUB only. Left blank, it is guessed from the name.
where.role: EPUB only, as a MARC relator code. Nothing else has anywhere to put it.
where.organization: The publisher in EPUB, the company in DOCX.
where.rights: The rights line in EPUB, the subject in PDF, the description in DOCX.

author.privacy: These fields are written into files you export and nowhere else. Nothing here is sent anywhere, and no address or account is asked for, because no export format has a place to put one.

project.title: Project
project.intro: Settings that belong to this novel, not to the app. They travel with the folder.
project.coverLabel: Open exports with a title page
project.coverHint: The title, your byline, and the publisher and rights lines when your author profile has them. A manuscript that arrives without one makes the reader work out whose it is from the filename.
project.colophonLabel: Close exports with this novel's record
project.colophonHint: The title, author, language, chapter and word count, and one line saying it was written here. Turn it off and that closing page is gone. The file's properties still name the program that made it, as every word processor does.
project.previewEmpty: Add an author in Settings → Author and it will appear here.
project.colophonThanks: Thank you for writing it here.
